expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides complete schema, migration, handler with error handling, and route setup

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: Handler accepts only { orderId, amountCents, reason }; no idempotency key parameter

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: No idempotency key or constraint implemented

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Both Order and Refund use bare String type without branded/distinct types

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
expectations.evidence: amountCents: Int in schema; validated and passed to Stripe as integer

expectations.text: Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Explicit check: if (amountCents > order.totalCents) rejects with 400

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: if (order.tenantId !== tenantId) check before Stripe call or database write

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Ends with 'Key design choices' section listing features, not explicit closure on impossible misuses

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Lists design choices (optimistic status, reason mapping) but never explicitly states what was deliberately left possible
